title: A hymn in Jaitsri
hook: Guru Arjan's Var in Jaitsri opens with a salok: whole at the beginning, the middle and the end

segments.voice: Yesterday, Raga Jaitsri: the jewel in the heart and the Guru's hand on the forehead. Your line: quiet strength.

Beginning, middle, end. Somewhere in school, someone wrote those three words on a board and said every story has them. The beginning is full of promise. The middle sags; it's where people get lost, bored or stuck. The end, if it's a good one, ties things up. A lot of life happens in some middle or other. Near the end of the Jaitsri section, Guru Arjan begins a Var, a ballad, and its very first salok says something surprising about all three.
screen: `BEGINNING, MIDDLE, END.` → `THE MIDDLE SAGS.` → `A VAR BEGINS IN JAITSRI.`

segments.voice: A Var in the Granth is a ballad made of pauris, stanzas, with saloks, short verses, set before them, like small lamps carried ahead of each stanza. This one, Jaitsri ki Var, is Guru Arjan's, mahala five. Its opening salok begins: aad pooran, madh pooran, ant pooran, parmesurah. Aad: the beginning. Madh: the middle. Ant: the end. Pooran: full, whole, complete. In paraphrase: whole at the beginning, whole in the middle, whole at the end, is the Supreme Lord. Then: the saints remember the one who pervades everywhere, and Nanak calls that one the destroyer of wrongs, the Lord of the world. Look at the word in the middle. Madh pooran. Whole in the middle. That's where any story feels least whole: the middle of a long illness, of a degree, of grief, of an ordinary Wednesday. The salok doesn't say God is waiting at the end once you get through. It says the middle is just as full as the start and the finish. That's where this Var's strength comes from. Not a burst of courage for the big moment, but a fullness that doesn't thin out halfway, and the Var goes on, stanza by stanza, built on that first promise. Strength in jaitsri is the strength of the middle.
screen: `A VAR: STANZAS WITH SALOKS BEFORE THEM.` · `AAD, MADH, ANT: BEGINNING, MIDDLE, END.` · `POORAN: WHOLE, AT EVERY POINT.` · `THE MIDDLE IS FULL TOO.` · then, large: `STRENGTH IN JAITSRI.`

segments.voice: Notice the beginning of a breath, cool air coming in, and the end of it, warm air going out, then the small pause at the top where nothing seems to happen, and rest there, breath after breath. Then think of one thing in your life that's in its middle right now, unfinished, and let it be whole for the length of a breath, with Waheguru in each pause if you pray.
A hymn in Jaitsri. Guru Arjan's Var, which opens with a salok: whole at the beginning, whole in the middle, whole at the end. Today's word.
Your line: strength in jaitsri. The middle is full too, not only the ends. Day one thousand eighty-seven.
